title: MISLEADING MOBILE APPLICATIONS
body_text:
The Ministry of Home Affairs has set up the ‘Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre’ (I4C) as an attached office to deal with all types of cyber crimes in the country, in a coordinated and comprehensive manner.
The ‘National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal’ (NCRP) ( https://cybercrime.gov.in ) has been launched, as a part of the I4C, to enable public to report incidents pertaining to all types of cyber crimes, with special focus on cyber crimes against women and children.
‘Sahyog’ Portal has been launched to expedite the process of sending notices to IT intermediaries by the Appropriate Government or its agency under clause (b) of sub-section (3) of section 79 of the IT Act, 2000 to facilitate the removal or disabling of access to any information, data or communication link being used to commit an unlawful act. Till 30.06.2026, a total of 3718 mobile apps including fraudulent loan apps have been blocked by I4C under Section 69(A), Section 79(3)(b) of IT Act 2000.
The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ (CFCFRMS), under I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the fraudsters. As per CFCFRMS operated by I4C, till 30.06.2026, financial amount of more than Rs. 11,158 Crore has been saved in more than 32.80 lakh complaints.
A Suspect Registry of identifiers of cyber criminals has been launched by I4C on 10.09.2024 in collaboration with Banks/Financial Institutions. Till 30.06.2026, more than 30.48 lakh suspect identifier data received from Banks and 32.08 lakh Layer 1 mule accounts have been shared with the participating entities of Suspect Registry and declined transactions worth Rs. 25,698 crores. Till 30.06.2026, more than 15.75 lakhs SIM cards and 5.77 lakhs IMEIs as reported by Police authorities have been blocked by Government of India.
To strengthen the operational efficiency and ensure uniformity in handling cybercrime complaints, the Ministry has issued a comprehensive Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for NCRP-CFCFRMS. The SOP lays down a standardized framework for complaint processing, bank coordination, grievance redressal, removal of lien markings, and restoration of defrauded funds to rightful claimants based on complaints received through the NCRP. Money Restoration Module for expeditious restoration of defrauded money to the victims and Grievance Redressal Module for timely attending to the grievances relating to freezing of the bank accounts and lien marking of the amount, have been made functional from April, 2026.
To further spread awareness on cyber crime, the Central Government has   taken   steps   which,    inter-alia,    include;   caller    tune   campaign, dissemination of messages through SMS, I4C social media account i.e. X (formerly Twitter) (@CyberDost), Facebook(CyberDostI4C), Instagram (CyberDostI4C), Telegram(cyberdosti4c),    SMS    campaign,    TV    campaign,    Radio campaign, School Campaign, advertisement in cinema halls, celebrity endorsement, IPL campaign, engaged MyGov for publicity in multiple mediums,  organizing Cyber Safety and Security Awareness weeks in association with States/UTs, publishing of Handbook for Adolescents/Students, digital displays on railway stations and airports across, etc.
This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, MoS Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar detailed the government's cybercrime infrastructure under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), including the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, Sahyog Portal, and Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS). As of 30.06.2026, 3,718 fraudulent apps had been blocked, over Rs 11,158 crore saved across 32.80 lakh complaints via CFCFRMS, and a Suspect Registry had blocked lakhs of SIMs and IMEIs while flagging mule accounts worth Rs 25,698 crore in declined transactions. The Ministry also issued a new SOP for complaint processing and fund restoration, and listed multiple public awareness campaigns against cyber fraud.
enrichment.context:
Cybercrime, especially financial fraud and misuse of mobile apps for phishing and predatory lending, has surged in India alongside rapid digital and financial inclusion. Since cybercrime falls largely under the State List but requires coordinated national response due to its cross-jurisdictional nature, MHA established I4C in 2018 to serve as a nodal coordination body, supporting states with technical infrastructure, threat intelligence, and portals like NCRP (2019) and CFCFRMS (2021). The Suspect Registry, launched in 2024, represents a newer effort to proactively flag repeat offenders and mule accounts using data shared by banks, addressing the problem of money mules who receive and launder defrauded funds.

The blocking of apps under Section 69A (content blocking) and Section 79(3)(b) (intermediary liability/safe harbour) of the IT Act 2000, and the Sahyog Portal for streamlining takedown notices, reflect the government's expanding use of IT Act provisions to regulate digital platforms and intermediaries, a subject of ongoing debate around due process, free speech, and platform accountability. Similarly, the new SOP for fund restoration and grievance redressal addresses a long-standing citizen grievance about delays and account freezes when reporting financial fraud, aligning with the broader push for improved grievance redressal mechanisms in digital governance.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre' (I4C) functions under which Ministry?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states I4C is an attached office of the Ministry of Home Affairs, set up to coordinate action against cybercrime nationally.

prelims_questions.question: Under which section(s) of the Information Technology Act, 2000 have fraudulent mobile applications been blocked by I4C, as per the release?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that 3,718 mobile apps have been blocked by I4C under Section 69(A) and Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, 2000, which deal with blocking of content and intermediary due diligence/takedown obligations respectively.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the institutional mechanisms established by India to combat cybercrime and financial fraud in the digital ecosystem. Evaluate their effectiveness and suggest measures for improvement.

mains_questions.question: Examine the role of intermediary liability provisions under the Information Technology Act, 2000 in regulating harmful online content, while balancing concerns of due process and freedom of expression.
